title: Claude W/ Remotion, animate skill, and PixelLab.ai for quickly putting together cutscenes.
author: CouldaBeen_TheBest
selftext:
Hi, not sure if people are already using this, but I wanted to share a proof of concept I created recently combining AI video editing with pixel assets for cutscene creation. I gave Claude an initial prompt detailing the specifics of the setting in question, a planet from one of my games, and instructed it to use Remotion in conjunction with generated assets to make this video.

Claude created a plan with individual cuts and timings based on what I asked for, incorporated my feedback, and prepared mockups for the pixel art generation, then edited together the assets using Remotion. Each cut gets its own .tsx file and the score was built by Claude using Python.

My prompts were not particularly deep here:

"I want to have this cloud session create animated content using remotion, animated via javascript https://github.com/cth9191/animate, asset generation via pixellab.ai midjourney & chatgpt pro. The goal is to produce personal animations and video content. Multiple topics and genres will be covered, but the initial test project is to create a short animation with a backing audio track. More details after repo and dependencies are configured."

"https://github.com/remotion-dev/remotion

Providing a link to the remotion repo if needed"

and finally:

"For the test run, the setting is on a planet that is 100% covered in city. A megalopolis planet called New Calidonia. This animated intro sequence should demonstrate daily life on the planet, describing both the fantastical elements and the mundane. A dog man and a robot argue over a parking space, a massively hairy alien hangs laundry on a balcony, an empty playground is built around a hologram of a tree. Each shot should be simple, short, and have some camera movement involved. Pixel art aesthetic is mandatory."

comments.author: janLolin
comments.body: for the love of god please align your pixel art

replies.author: CouldaBeen_TheBest
replies.body: You're right, it's a total mess. But the goal was just to prove the idea. The sprites are especially tacky so for my next attempt I would refine the visuals significantly more.
